lemma_statement: theorem isWeierstrassModel_unique (W : WeierstrassCurve R) [W.IsElliptic] {X X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)} {x₀ : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of R)} {x₀' : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X'} (hs : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f) (hs' : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f') (h : IsWeierstrassModel W X f x₀) (h' : IsWeierstrassModel W X' f' x₀') : ∃ e : X ≅ X', e.hom ≫ f' = f ∧ x₀ ≫ e.hom = x₀'
b2_reason: IsWeierstrassModel's points clause is a BARE pointed Equiv (cardinality only, DEF-7 form). Over R = ℚ take E, E' ℚ-isogenous non-isomorphic elliptic curves of positive rank (2-isogeny pair y²=x³−36x / y²=x³+144x, n=6 congruent). A ℚ-isogeny φ and its dual give |E(K)| ≤ deg·|E'(K)| and conversely for every ℚ-algebra field K; both sets are infinite (rank ≥ 1 is isogeny-invariant), so the cardinals agree for EVERY K and a pointed bijection exists. Hence X' := projModel E' satisfies IsWeierstrassModel (E-data) with smoothness, but the concluded pointed iso projModel E ≅ projModel E' over Spec ℚ would make E ≅ E' as elliptic curves (pointed iso + rigidity) — contradiction. KM 2.2.5 (full text now mined, printed pp. 68-69) is uniqueness of ADAPTED COORDINATES x,y for a FIXED (E/S, ω) — up to x ↦ x+a, y ↦ y+ax+b — not reconstruction of the scheme from field-point counts; the ticket statement is strictly stronger than the source and false. FIX OPTIONS for owner: (1) strengthen points to a K-NATURAL family of bijections (functor of points on ℚ-algebra fields; kills the cardinality slack — isogeny bijections are not natural), or (2) define the model property as ∃ pointed iso to projModel W (uniqueness becomes trivial, content moves to a characterization theorem), or (3) restate T-A4 in KM's actual form: uniqueness of the Weierstrass presentation of a FIXED pointed smooth proper curve, i.e. two Weierstrass data W₁ W₂ with pointed-isomorphic projModels are related by VariableChange (needs BB-RR).
counterexample: R = ℚ; W = Weierstrass data of E : y² = x³ − 36x (rank 1); X' = projModel of E' : y² = x³ + 144x (2-isogenous, E' ≇ E — distinct minimal models); both satisfy the hypotheses, conclusion forces E ≅ E'.

lemma_statement: theorem representable_iff (P : ModuliProblem R) : P.Representable ↔ P.RelativelyRepresentable ∧ P.Rigid
b2_reason: Statement (= Loeffler Thm 3.7.4 verbatim) is unsupported by either source's proof: KM's SCHOLIE (4.7.0) carries the hypothesis 'relatively representable AND AFFINE over (Ell)', which KM's proof uses three times — book p.112 (M(P,delta) affine over affine M(delta) => absolutely affine), p.113 ('Because M(P,delta) is affine, the quotient M(P,delta)/G exists'), p.114 (alpha_univ descends 'because P is relatively affine', SGA I VIII 7.8). lemma_statement: theorem gammaHNaive_relativelyRepresentable (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (H : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod N))) (hinv : IsUnit (N : R)) : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).RelativelyRepresentable ∧ ∀ X : EllObj R, ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ X.base), IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧ ∀ {T} (g : T ⟶ X.base), Nonempty ({ h : T ⟶ Z // h ≫ f = g } ≃ (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).obj (Opposite.op (X.pullbackAlong g)))
b2_reason: FALSE for every H ≠ ⊥. `gammaHNaiveProblem R N H` is defined as *global* H-orbits of naive full-level-N structures, `P_H(E/S) := {H-orbits of Isom((Z/N)^2, E[N]) over S}`. This presheaf is NOT a Zariski (or fppf) sheaf, hence not relatively representable: over `T = X.base ⊔ X.base` (codiagonal g : T → X.base, gᵢ = 𝟙), the diagonal glue [(L,L)] and the twisted glue [(L, γ·L)] (γ ≠ 1 in H, glSmul the GL₂-action) have equal restriction to each summand ([L]=[L] and [L]=[γ·L] as H-orbits, since γ·L ∈ H·L) yet are distinct global sections when the H-action is free — a descent/separatedness failure. (A counting variant over étale covers kills the étale conjunct too.) SOURCES CONCUR it is a transcription slip: Loeffler Fact 3.8.1 pins P_H(E/k̄) as H-orbits only on ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED k̄ (geometric points), never as a naive presheaf on all S; his §3.6 notes the naive orbit map is 'neither injective nor surjective'; KM DEFINES P_H as the quotient moduli problem `[Γ(N)]/H` of Chapter 7 §7.1 (verbatim below), NOT as naive orbits. KM 7.1.2 (print p.187, pdf 198): 𝒫' = 𝒫/G iff (Q1) G operates trivially on 𝒫', and (Q2) for every representable δ étale over (Ell/R), 𝕸(δ,𝒫)/G exists and maps isomorphically to 𝕸(δ,𝒫') [equivalently (𝒫_{E/S})/G ≅ (𝒫'_{E/S})]. KM THEOREM 7.1.3(1),(2),(4): for 𝒫 relatively representable and affine over (Ell/R) with G finite acting, 𝒫/G exists as a relatively representable moduli problem affine over (Ell/R); if G operates freely, 𝒫 is an étale G-torsor over 𝒫/G; 𝒫 → 𝒫/G is finite. FIX (owner-delegated, B2 EVENT #2): repoint T-H4/T-H6 at the KM-7.1.2 quotient problem `P_H = [Γ(N)]/H` (corrected statements STAGED in Moduli/GammaHRepresentability.lean: gammaH_relativelyRepresentable, gammaHNaive_toQuotient, gammaH_representable_of_rigid, with the H=⊥ salvage gammaHNaive_relativelyRepresentable_bot PROVEN). The falsity is LOCKED into the library by gammaHNaiveProblem_not_relativelyRepresentable (the codiagonal counterexample, sorry-free in its own proof; residual sorryAx via gated FullLevelPt/glSmul helpers, follow-up). The naive statement is NOT deleted from GammaH.lean (theorem_statement_protected); it stands as the documented non-goal.
counterexample: H ≠ ⊥ (pick γ ∈ H, γ ≠ 1); T = X.base ⊔ X.base with codiagonal g; sections [(L,L)] and [(L, glSmul γ L)] of P_H over T restrict equally on each summand (H-orbit equality) but differ globally when the H-action on Isom is free — so P_H is not a sheaf, hence not relatively representable. Formalized: gammaHNaiveProblem_not_relativelyRepresentable.

lemma_statement: theorem gammaHNaive_representable_of_rigid (N)(H)(hinv)(hrig : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).Rigid) : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).Representable ∧ ∀ X, Nonempty (RepresentableBy X) → Smooth ∧ IsAffineHom
b2_reason: Rigid→Representable is asserted for the H-ORBIT-PRESHEAF, but representable presheaves are fppf sheaves and the orbit presheaf fails the fppf sheaf axiom at rigid H. Take H = unipotent upper-triangular (rigid for N ≥ 4: preimage torsion-free — trace ≡ 2 mod N forces no elliptic elements, -1 excluded for N ≥ 3). Twisted complement: E/ℚ with rational P of order N generating E(ℚ)[N], and Galois acting on any complement lift Q by σQ = Q + b_σ·P with nontrivial cocycle b (cyclic twist class; classical existence). Over the cyclic cover L the pair (P,Q) is an honest presheaf section; its two pullbacks to L⊗L agree as H-orbits (cocycle condition), but no section over ℚ exists (a ℚ-orbit-representative would need a RATIONAL Q). Sheaf gluing fails ⟹ not representable ⟹ the implication is false as stated. In-tree corroboration: [GHC3] (GammaHRep:3601+) records the orbit-presheaf/quotient comparison is bijective only over k̄ and NOT an isomorphism of problems for H ≠ ⊥.
counterexample: H = {(1,*;0,1)} ≤ GL₂(ℤ/N), N ≥ 4; E/ℚ with E(ℚ)[N] = ⟨P⟩ ≅ ℤ/N and complement twisted by a nontrivial cyclic cocycle; cover Spec L → Spec ℚ. Fix options: (a) RECOMMENDED restate at qpd.prob (sheaf quotient — the true statement is the existing gammaH_representable interface, proven modulo the engine); (b) add fppf-sheafiness of the orbit presheaf as a hypothesis; (c) weaken to geometric points per GHC3.

lemma_statement: theorem orderedBaseCech_residueField_exact_of_fibre_trivial {R} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {X : Scheme} [IsNoetherian X] [X.IsSeparated] {pi : X -> Spec (.of R)} [LocallyOfFinitePresentation pi] [IsProper pi] [Flat pi] (hpi : UniversallyOConnected pi) {M : X.Modules} (hM : IsInvertible M) {iota} [Fintype iota] [LinearOrder iota] (U : iota -> X.Opens) (hU : IsOpenCover U) (hUaff : forall i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (p : Ideal Gamma(Spec (.of R), top)) [p.IsPrime] (hfib : fibrewise trivial) : forall q, q < Fintype.card iota -> Function.Exact ((C.d q (q+1)).hom.baseChange p.ResidueField) ((C.d (q+1) (q+2)).hom.baseChange p.ResidueField)
b2_reason: FALSE. Function.Exact at index q asserts exactness of the base-changed ordered Cech complex at position q+1, i.e. H^{q+1}(X_p, M_p) = 0 for all q < card iota. Fibrewise TRIVIALITY gives M_p iso O_{X_p}, and on a genus-1 fibre H^1(E_p, O) = kappa(p) is NONZERO, so exactness at position 1 fails. The tree's own results confirm the boundary: sectionPoleSheafPower_residueField_orderedBaseCech_exactAt_succ (EllipticCurve/PoleSheafBaseCechHigher.lean:295) proves positive-degree exactness ONLY for O(n[0]) with hn : 1 <= n, i.e. only for ample positive twists where H^1 vanishes; n = 0 (the trivial sheaf) is excluded precisely because H^1(E,O) = k. Stacks 0EX7 does not need full exactness either: it needs h^0(X_s, M_s) constant = 1, i.e. constant KERNEL rank of d^0, which is a different statement. Replanned into KM-SEESAW-1' (kernel finrank 1 at every prime) + KM-SEESAW-2' (constant kernel rank + reduced base => ker d^0 invertible and the counit is an iso); the parent 0EX7 statement is TRUE and unchanged.
counterexample: R = k a field, X = E an elliptic curve over k, M = O_E (trivial, hence fibrewise trivial), p = 0 the unique prime, U any finite affine cover with card iota >= 2. Then exactness at position 1 of the base-changed ordered Cech complex would give H^1(E, O_E) = 0, but H^1(E, O_E) = k since the genus is 1.

lemma_statement: theorem exists_pullback_iso_of_kernel_finrank {X S : Scheme} [IsAffine S] [IsReduced S] [IsNoetherian X] [X.IsSeparated] {pi : X -> S} [LocallyOfFinitePresentation pi] [IsProper pi] [Flat pi] (hpi : UniversallyOConnected pi) {M : X.Modules} (hM : IsInvertible M) {iota} [Fintype iota] [LinearOrder iota] (U : iota -> X.Opens) (hU : IsOpenCover U) (hUaff : forall i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hrank : forall (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra Gamma(S,top) K], Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker (((orderedBaseCechComplex pi M U).d 0 1).hom.baseChange K)) = 1) : exists N : S.Modules, IsInvertible N and Nonempty (M iso (Modules.pullback pi).obj N)
b2_reason: FALSE. The hypothesis hrank says only that h^0(X_s, M_s) = 1 at every field-valued point. That is strictly WEAKER than the fibrewise triviality M_s iso O_{X_s} that Stacks 0EX7 actually assumes, and it does not imply the conclusion. 0EX7's mechanism needs BOTH: constant h^0 (for local freeness of pi_* M over a reduced base) AND fibrewise triviality (so that the generator of Gamma(X_s, M_s) is NOWHERE VANISHING, which is what makes the counit pi^* pi_* M -> M an isomorphism rather than merely injective). Replacing fibrewise triviality by its numerical consequence h^0 = 1 loses exactly the nowhere-vanishing information. This is the SAME error shape as the earlier KM-SEESAW-1 B2 in this file: substituting a cohomological dimension for a geometric hypothesis. FIX: the descent leaf must retain hfib alongside hrank; hrank alone supplies local freeness, hfib supplies surjectivity of the counit.
counterexample: S = Spec k for a field k, X = E an elliptic curve over k (proper, flat, finite presentation, geometrically integral fibres, Gamma(E,O) = k so UniversallyOConnected holds, and Spec k is reduced). Take M = O_E(P) for a rational point P != 0. Riemann-Roch on genus 1 with deg D = 1 > 2g-2 = 0 gives h^1 = 0 and h^0 = deg D + 1 - g = 1, and the same after any field extension, so hrank holds. But the conclusion would give M iso pi^* N with N invertible on Spec k, hence N iso O and O_E(P) iso O_E — false, since O_E(P) has degree 1 and O_E has degree 0. Concretely the counit pi^* pi_* O_E(P) -> O_E(P) is the inclusion O_E -> O_E(P), injective and NOT surjective: the generator of Gamma(O_E(P)) is the image of 1, whose zero divisor is P.

lemma_statement: From `f : (projModel W).functionField` with `projectiveDivisorOf f = kappaDivisor W (P+Q) - kappaDivisor W P - kappaDivisor W Q`, produce a SquareChartData for the four section ideals.
b2_reason: SCOPE ERROR in the ticket's field input. HasseWeil's `projectiveDivisorOf` is indexed by `SmoothPlaneCurve.SmoothPoint`, i.e. the k-RATIONAL affine points plus infinity. Over a non-algebraically-closed k it does not see closed points of degree > 1, so `ProjIsPrincipal` pins f only up to a factor whose divisor is supported at those invisible points. Building the chart data from such an f is therefore unsound: the local generators it produces need not be the right ones.
counterexample: Over k not algebraically closed, let S, S-bar be conjugate quadratic points and U, U-bar another conjugate pair with the same trace. The function with divisor (S)+(S-bar)-(U)-(U-bar) is invisible to `projectiveDivisorOf` (its divisor is supported off the rational points), so f is not determined and multiplying by it changes the chart generators without changing the recorded projective divisor.
resolution: State the leaf WITHOUT the divisor witness as a hypothesis (done). Close it either by (a) the explicit chord-and-vertical function read off the two Weierstrass charts, which produces cover, generators and rational function TOGETHER -- necessary because pointwise principality fixes generators only up to a per-chart unit and those units do not cancel in the cocycle -- or (b) strengthening `HasseWeil.Curves.MillerHypothesis` from rational points to all closed points. Route (a) also solves the generator problem; route (b) does not.
